items.title: Marvel Fans Say Avengers: Endgame Encore's Extra 4 Minutes Risk Being 'Really Oversold', After Directors Insist Movie is 'Required Viewing for Following The Story in Doomsday'
items.description: We all love Avengers: Endgame, but some Marvel fans are now suggesting that the four minutes of footage added to its upcoming Encore re-release risk being oversold by its directors.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
We all love Avengers: Endgame, but some Marvel fans are now suggesting that the four minutes of footage added to its upcoming Encore re-release risk being oversold by its directors.

Endgame is one of the best Marvel movies of all time — perhaps the best — and so it's not surprising to see it return to theaters this fall ahead of Avengers: Doomsday's arrival. Not only will this new chance to watch the film inject a few more million into its box office total (perhaps enough to overtake Avatar once again!), the experience will likely remind cinema audiences of the excitement felt at the close of the Infinity Saga, as a decade of storytelling came to a natural conclusion.

But after the reveal that Avengers: Endgame Encore will be just four minutes longer than the movie's original runtime, fans are revisiting recent comments by directors Joe and Anthony Russo — who suggested that an Endgame watch (or rewatch) was "required viewing" to follow Doomsday's own story — with a healthy dose of scepticism.

A clip of the Russos discussing Avengers: Endgame Encore at San Diego Comic-Con last month is now being shared widely on social media, where the duo discussed why they thought fans should see the film again with Fandango.

"It's going to connect the story of the two movies," Joe Russo said of Avengers: Endgame Encore. "There's a natural progression from Endgame into Doomsday, which is also inclusive of all the other stories that have been playing out.

"But I think it's important to see Endgame in theaters again for two reasons," he continued. "One, if you want to have a lot of fun cheering and screaming and reliving all the emotions you had the first time you saw it. Two, I think it's required viewing for following the story in Doomsday.

"If you saw Endgame when it was originally released, you couldn't see this coming," Anthony Russo added.

Anthony and Joe Russo break down what fans can expect to see in Avengers Endgame: Encore.

Tickets are on sale NOW! Assemble your friends, and get your tickets now👇 https://t.co/CgcsDpHycS pic.twitter.com/AaFAk5c1rf

— Fandango (@Fandango) August 25, 2026

Marvel has not detailed what the new footage added to Avengers: Endgame Encore will comprise, though there's a growing sense among fans that it is likely to be scenes shot during Avengers: Doomsday's production that may also end up within Doomsday itself. Many fans believe this is likely to focus on the journey of Steve Rogers — perhaps showing him returning the Infinity Stones, or returning home to Peggy Carter afterwards, only for his peace and quiet to be swiftly disturbed.

In general, though, there's a sense among fans that Marvel would not actually make Avengers: Doomsday incomprehensible without prior MCU knowledge, and certainly not without actually requiring fans to rewatch a movie that released years ago with a few minutes of extras added on. Doomsday will do very well at the box office regardless, of course, but would hardly benefit if its plot hinged on something that only those who attended a screening of Endgame Encore could understand.

"It's literally four extra minutes of footage that will be in a YouTube short within two days," wrote one Marvel fan, in the top comment of a new and lengthy reddit thread discussing the Russo's claims. "I mean I'm probably still gonna go see it just because Endgame was great, and I'd love to see it again in Dolby, but they are really overselling this extra footage, I think."

"Yeah. Not getting a babysitter," a second fan wrote. "Spending $30-$40 for four minutes of footage. A little tone deaf to say 'required viewing'. I'll wait for the leaks."

"Normal fans aren't going to go shell out $100 for something they can watch for free on Disney+," wrote another fan. "They are going to be unaware there's a few minutes of additional footage. They'll be there for Doomsday though."

"The last thing this world needs is f***ing DLC for movies," added yet another.

"What do you expect them to say?" countered another fan. "'Skip this one guys, it's only 4 extra minutes and you can just watch a recap video on YouTube.' Like of course they're gonna oversell it lol it's their job."

"Am I gonna go see it? Yes," one fan wrote on X/Twitter. "But are you guys false advertising infinity vision and just trying to make more money because it's only [four] minutes, absolutely."

Marvel has currently made no suggestion it will detail exactly what its new Encore footage will contain, likely meaning audiences will find out for themselves when the film's re-release rolls around next month. Will you be going as well? Avengers: Endgame Encore arrives in theaters on September 25 (with Iron Man and Infinity Gauntlet popcorn buckets) before Avengers: Doomsday finally lands on December 18.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Xbox and IKEA Furniture Collaboration Includes Thumbstick Stools, Tables, and D-Pad Accessories
items.description: IKEA has unveiled a range of official Xbox furniture, including gaming chairs, display stands and cozy-looking D-pad cushion.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
IKEA has unveiled a range of official Xbox furniture, including gaming chairs, display stands and cozy-looking D-pad cushions.

The range goes on sale in the U.K. from October via the retailer's website and in IKEA stores, and is officially named "YXSTABY" — a name I won't try and pronounce out loud.

In a press release sent to IGN today, IKEA said that YXSTABY reflected "an era where gaming furniture is moving out of teen bedrooms and man caves and into the mainstream living room."

Created together by Xbox and IKEA designers, the nine-piece collection includes functional furniture such as controller display boxes, TV stands on castors, and a side table to store all your gaming accessories.

There are also more bizarre-looking additions, such as green and black "gaming Thumbstick stools", which really do look like the sticks of an Xbox controller at giant size. IKEA says these were developed using the controller's original 3D design files for maximum authenticity. It even tilts as you lean, echoing the thumbstick's motion to keep gamers "comfortably engaged during intense sessions."

My favorite item is probably the green gaming D-pad cushion, although I do also rather like the D-pad platter, themed after the concave metal D-pad on Xbox Elite pads.

"At Xbox, we think a lot about what helps players feel immersed in a game," said Carl Ledbetter, Xbox Head of Design. "The hardware is an important part of that, but so is the world you create around it. Working with IKEA gave us the opportunity to design for the entire gaming experience at home, from the screen to the space around it."

The range is currently on display on Xbox's booth over at Gamescom, ahead of its wider launch in a couple of months. Tempted? You could be leaning forward on your thumbstick stool just in time for GTA 6, or settling down on your D-pad cushion waiting for Fable.

The full range and its pricing is listed just below:

items.title: LEGO Super Mario Minifigure Sets Unveiled, Including Bowser's Castle and Mario Kart
items.description: LEGO has finally revealed its Super Mario range that will include minifigures for the first time, including playsets for Bowser's Castle and numerous Mario Kart vehicles.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
LEGO has finally revealed its Super Mario range that will include minifigures for the first time, including playsets for Bowser's Castle and numerous Mario Kart vehicles.

Super Mario has been appearing in LEGO sets for years, though mostly as part of the company's bigger-scale range designed to work with the interactive Super Mario toy unit.

That experiment now seems to over, however, with the long-awaited rollout of Super Mario sets scaled to minifigure size. And indeed, these will also include a growing range of Mario minifigures, with Luigi, Peach, Toad, Yoshi, Koopa Troopa, and Bowser Jr. all glimpsed in this first wave, as well as a Bowser big fig. The range will all be available from January 1, 2027.

LEGO Super Mario Minifigure range

  • Mario's Pipe Jump (72052) – 61 pieces, $9.99
  • Racing with Mario (72054) – 84 pieces, $14.99
  • Mario's Beach Adventures (72055) – 196 pieces, $19.99
  • Luigi & Bowser Jr.'s Race (72056) – 104 pieces, $29.99
  • Yoshi at Mario's House (72057) – 147 pieces, $39.99
  • Bowser's Rumbling Race (72058) – 409 pieces, $59.99
  • Fire Mario & Bowser's Castle (72060) – 850 pieces, $99.99
  • Fire Luigi vs. Koopa Troopa Battle (72061) – 241 pieces, $29.99

The range begins with Mario's Pipe Jump (72052), a 61-piece set priced at $9.99 that features a Mario minifigure, dinky Goomba element and large green warp pipe. Next up is Racing with Mario (72054), an 84-piece set for $14.99 that features a Mario minifigure and the plumber's classic kart. Green and red shells are also included, as is a banana.

Mario's Beach Adventures (72055) sees the hero take some downtime by the sea. This 196-piece set sells for $19.99 and includes a Mario in swim trunks minifigure (no, he doesn't have nipples), plus a buildable snack bar, lounger and giant enemy crab.

Luigi & Bowser Jr.'s Race (72056) is essentially a larger version of the previous Racing with Mario set, except with both Luigi and Bowser Jr. Both characters are included as minifigures, alongside their karts and accessories. This is a 104-piece set that will sell for $29.99.

Moving onto the slightly bigger sets, Yoshi at Mario's House (72057) is a 147-piece build that sells for $39.99. Included here are Mario and a slightly awkward-looking Yoshi minifigure, plus a goomba.

Bowser's Rumbling Race (72058) is another Mario Kart set, this time with 409 pieces for $59.99. Here, you can expand your starting lineup with karts for Toad, Bowser, Goomba and Mario Kart World's fan-favorite Cow. The first two characters are minifigures, while the latter is a buildable design.

The biggest set in this starting wave is Fire Mario & Bowser's Castle, which will weigh in at 850 pieces and sell for $99.99. This features Fire Mario, Peach and Koopa Trooper minifigures, the Bowser big fig and a goomba. It's a cool-looking design, even if LEGO is clearly making us wait for the Peach's Castle set we all really want.

Lastly, Fire Luigi vs. Koopa Troopa Battle (72061) is a smaller 241-piece set featuring, unsurprisingly, Fire Luigi and a Koopa Troopa minifigures.

"The new LEGO minifigures mark a refreshed LEGO Super Mario theme, newly centred on creative LEGO minifigure roleplay action," LEGO stated in a press release today. "The refresh of the Super Mario theme will see building experiences arriving for LEGO Super Mario centred on creative LEGO minifigure roleplay, featuring iconic characters, karts, and environments from the Super Mario and Mario Kart universe."

So, which will you be picking up?

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Atari Is Re-Releasing 39 Atari 2600 Games on Working, Physical Cartridges
items.description: Atari has today announced a new physical game collaboration with Activision called the Atari x Activision Collection, reuniting Activision with Atari after almost 50 years.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Atari has today announced a new physical game collaboration with Activision called the Atari x Activision Collection. The unexpected project reunites Activision with Atari after almost 50 years.

The full set of working, physical game cartridges includes 39 classic Activision games, like Pitfall!, River Raid, and Kaboom!, and there will be three ways to purchase them.

Individual, “Standard Edition” versions of 12 of the games will be available from November for USD$35 each. The 12 games include Pitfall!, River Raid, Megamania, Enduro, Kaboom!, H.E.R.O., Pressure Cooker, Private Eye, River Raid II, Keystone Kapers, The Activision Decathlon, and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns (although Atari notes The Activision Decathlon and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns will actually ship at a later date than the other titles). The Standard Edition games feature full packaging and a printed, colour manual inspired by the original releases. They’ll be compatible with Atari 2600+ and Atari 7800+ consoles, as well as original Atari 2600 and 7800 hardware.

There will also be four box sets available, which will widen the collection to the full 39 games. The first of the four box sets (which are dubbed Treasure, Speed, Secrets, and Victory) will be available from late November, with the remaining three will follow over the first three quarters of 2027. These will be available via pre-orders at atari.com for USD$250. A complete collection of all 39 games (which will reportedly include a yet-to-be-announced “collectible item”) will also be sold via pre-order for USD$1000.

“In 1979, a group of Atari programmers set out to prove that great games could come from independent creators and ended up changing the industry forever,” said Atari’s VP of hardware Matt Burnett in a comment published in conjunction with today’s announcement. “The Atari x Activision Collection brings that legacy to life through the games themselves, giving fans an opportunity to experience, collect and preserve the work of the developers who helped establish a new model for the video game industry.”

The resurrection of fresh, physical versions of Activision’s very oldest games comes as an interesting surprise amid the bleak times collectors of physical media are currently otherwise facing, and with PlayStation maintaining its decision to discontinue physical discs in the near future won’t have any negative impact on its business either now or in the future.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Wilderings: The Lost Spring Gameplay Trailer Reveals Volcanic Biome, a Moth Boss, and a Version 1.0 Release Window
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
At gamescom 2026, Kabam and Herobeat Studios revealed a brand-new gameplay trailer for Wilderings that unveiled a fiery new Volcanic biome, a first look at Röhe the Moth Boss, and the confirmation that the open-world action-adventure game will be launching its Version 1.0 update in spring 2027.

Wilderings, which also encourages exploration and features fast-paced action, roguelite progression, and creature collecting, follows Abi and her companion Rif as they traverse a fractured world that is quickly being consumed by darkness.

To help in her journey, she will discover and adopt mysterious creatures known as Hântu, which she can use to help her fight, get through tough spots with their abilities, and to move about the world. In this new Volcanic biome, Abi will run into at least three Hântu, Razzle (explosive projectiles that burn and multiply), Mokul (summons pyroclastic rain that scorches an area), and Furioso (throws magma that spreads between enemies).

As for Röhe, this Moth Boss is actually a young hunter from the Frostlands who will challenge Abi in this new region. To make it through the test set in a "magma-lit arena," Abi will have to perfet her movement, combat skills, and Hântu abilities.

For those at gamescom, Wilderings: The Lost Spring will be available to play at the Indie Arena Booth, Hall 10.2 Booth F010g - E019, from August 26-30.

For more, check out everything announced from Opening Night Live and what else to expect from the rest of gamescom.

Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

items.title: Xbox Design Chief Reveals the Surprising Ikea Item That Shaped Every Console
items.description: Xbox design chief Carl Ledbetter reveals how an Ikea bookcase inspired the console’s design, as Xbox and Ikea launch the new YXSTABY furniture line.
items.author: Michael Peyton
items.content:
Gamescom kicks off today in Cologne, Germany, and among the many big game debuts, hands-on demos, and major announcements is a new kind of reveal: Xbox is partnering with Ikea to sell an exclusive set of Xbox-inspired furniture and accessories that you can buy starting this fall. But, according to Xbox, the new collection goes far beyond the typical gamer chair and desk setup.

Carl Ledbetter, head of design at Xbox, has been at Microsoft for more than 30 years (dating back to the days of the IntelliMouse) and is responsible for designing consoles like the Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S. Ledbetter led the charge with the Ikea collaboration and says the partnership isn’t as unusual as you might suspect .

I spoke to Ledbetter exclusively at gamescom ahead of the reveal of YXSTABY (get it?) a “nine-piece collection designed for gaming at home,” and found out that Xbox’s ties to Ikea go back further than you might expect.

An iconic Ikea bookcase influenced the Xbox shape

“The piece of furniture that we use as our de facto test for any console design is the Billy bookcase from Ikea,” Ledbetter says. “So believe it or not, it's a natural fit. I’ve spent all my time [at Xbox] looking at input, controllers, the console, how things fit into the home. [That] matters when you design a console, [the] horizontal and vertical position. [So] this goes back years. The philosophy that we share for designing products at Xbox and at Ikea are nearly identical. So it was like a love connection.”

IGN can exclusively reveal a look at the entire collection, which features nine pieces, including chairs with console pockets, thumbstick-shaped stools, a D-Pad inspired platter to hold your controller, X-shaped pillows, and more. Ledbetter says that planning a series of pieces intended to be picked up, sat on, leaned against, and otherwise interacted with came with a surprising challenge.

“Xbox and Ikea, they both have scale,” Ledbetter says. “We designed for millions of players around the world. Ikea’s already there. The thing that is different, at least for my team and designing this line, was taking into consideration the flat pack. So Ikea, of course [uses a flat pack] in order to ship these things all around the world. When you buy a console, the most you have to do is plug it in and turn it on. But in this case, you have some assembly required. It was just fascinating to work with them side by side and see how to problem-solve. That was pretty fun.”

Ledbetter says that, although bringing a collection of furniture to life is inherently different than building a new console, his overarching design philosophy didn’t change.

“First and foremost, the product's got to work,” Ledbetter says. “It has to solve real problems. Whether it's a controller or a piece of furniture, it's the same thing. The second thing is, for gamers, particularly when they're playing Xbox games at home, it's about immersion. It’s in the game you see on the screen and in the controller you hold in your hand. But if you think about it, it's everything around you. The products you sit on, the things that hold your TV, etc. We started talking about those challenges for players and immediately started coming up together with ideas. We tried to find balance.

“The question that the Ikea designers had for me was, ‘Carl, what are the iconic elements of Xbox?’ Number one is the controller. While we've improved it and changed it over time, it's very recognizable. And so there are elements that people interact with on the controller that they just sort of bubbled up to the top. The D-pad was one. So you see the D-pad platter, the D-pad pillow. And of course the thumbstick was just right there. It's such an interactive and engaging thing. We landed on the thumbstick stool.”

Xbox designer reveals the new YXSTABY furniture collection contains plenty of hidden details

Ledbetter says that for hardcore Xbox fans, there will be plenty of Easter eggs when the YXSTABY collection hits stores this fall.

“If you look at the TV stand or the monitor stand, if you look at the detailing that the designers have put on these products, they’re super clean,” Ledbetter says. “There's nothing extra. The materials are honest and authentic. Those same [XBOX] design qualities are used throughout the entire collection.

“They may not stand out immediately. We call it the second level read, third level read. You start to notice the subtleties of these things. There are some subtle things. If you look at the gaming chair, we used green stitching. It is super, super subtle, but for those who know, they'll know. They'll recognize these little qualities.”

The new Xbox furniture line will have plenty of accessibility features

Ledbetter, who contributed to the design of Xbox’s revolutionary adaptive controller, says designing YXSTABY for all gamers was just as important as throwing in subtle nods to hardcore fans.

“The more people who can use the product, the better,” Ledbetter says. “The gaming chair is designed for two types of gaming postures. The first one is just sitting up. It's the leaning forward posture. [For games like] Gears of War: E-Day, maybe you're getting sweaty and it's intense. And then what happens when you beat the boss? [You go back.] Also, what we found in the prototyping process of the pillow is you can actually take it and rest your arms when you play. It creates a really cool experience.

“[Another] accessible design is the monitor stand. You can put the monitor on it and it's more ergonomic, at eye level. So it gets you in a better posture. And then underneath you can put your mouse, keyboard, and a laptop under there. It can fit an Xbox Series S. And then it has all these configurable stands for your headset, for your cellphone. There's a spot in there to charge your controllers. So we really try to accommodate different people and what their needs are.”

Ledbetter would like to build an Xbox-inspired house

Throughout his long career at Microsoft, Ledbetter has had the chance to design a number of popular, iconic products whose form is immediately recognizable to gamers and non-gamers alike. And while he’s pleased with how the Ikea collaboration has turned out, he says there’s one major Xbox adaptation he’d still like to tackle if given the opportunity.

“The Xbox One X, when it came out, the Scorpio [edition] was the smallest and most powerful console we'd ever made,” Ledbetter says. “But if you look at that, it sort of has this layered design to it. It'd be fun to turn that into a home. [It could be] very inspired by [Frank Lloyd Wright's] Falling Water with little layers. [It makes sense because] the purity of the designs of our consoles are designed to be as expressive or quiet as people want them to be.”

YXSTABY is being unveiled this week at gamescom and will be available in Ikea stores and online this fall.

items.title: Konami Partners With Celebrity Kitty to Release Metal Gear Cat Toys at CatCon 2026
items.description: Konami is partnering up with a celebrity kitty named ‘one-eared Uno’ to debut a special Metal Gear cat toy collection available at CatCon 2026.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Konami is partnering up with a celebrity kitty named ‘one-eared Uno’ to debut a special Metal Gear cat toy collection available at CatCon 2026.

If you didn’t know there was a cat convention, now you do. CatCon is a yearly event that brings together cat lovers from all over the globe to Pasadena, California, featuring special exhibits, workshops, adoption drives, and meet-and-greets with celebrity cats.

One of those cats, affectionately named ‘one-eared Uno,’ and her owner, Kat Curtis, will host a special meet-and-greet event at the Konami booth at CatCon this year to celebrate the release of some special Metal Gear-themed cat toys.

These offerings include cat scratch boxes modeled after the iconic cardboard boxes that Big Boss and Old Snake use to sneak around without being detected by enemies, plush pet toys, and even cat collars inspired by Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker and Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots.

The lovable one-eared Uno with her adorable underbite was rescued by Kat as a stray, who found the kitty abandoned near a dumpster. The two now boast over five million followers on social media and are meeting fans at Catcon on October 12 at 2 PM PST.

CatCon takes place at the Pasadena Convention Center from October 10 - 11. Cat lovers will be able to score the Snake-approved merch for their kitties on those days only, both at the convention and online via the OKS Gear Shop.

What’s more, fans can win a chance to meet Uno at CatCon and get the exclusive Metal Gear merch if they visit the Konami booth at the convention and either: show they own the Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2, add the collection to their wishlist, or purchase the Metal Gear merchandise at the booth.

This collaboration might be off the wall, but given the sheer amount of absurdities that take place within the series, we can’t say that this partnership is totally out of left field. This limited-time partnership marks the launch of the Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2, a compilation of the classic stealth-action games that releases on August 17, 2026 for Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, XBOX Series X|S, and Steam.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: The First New Magic Puzzle of 2026 Is Now Available at Retailers
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
The first of the Series 6 Magic Puzzle Company puzzles is now available to buy at Amazon and Target. The Spooky Shire isn't even listed on the company's website yet, so it appears to be making its retail debut a bit early.

The Spooky Shire features original art from Kasey White and depicts a colorful scene full of ghosts, witches, skeletons, and a ton of cute little pumpkins. Like all Magic puzzles, it's made up of 1,000 pieces.

If you aren't already familiar with the Magic Puzzle Company, It's pretty easy to explain why its one of the best puzzle brands out there. The pieces are unique, the art is always incredible (not AI generated), and there's always a magical surpise waiting for you at the end.

These puzzles are also just really fun to put together. There's so many different things going on in each scene, which makes every newly added piece feel special. According to the product page, there are over 50 easter eggs to find as you put the puzzle together. You also get two art posters you can use as a reference.

When Will There Be More Series 6 Puzzles

It's hard to say exactly when the other two Series 6 puzzles will arrive, but it likely won't be any time soon. The first new Series 5 puzzle was released in August 2025, but the rest weren't made available until January 2026. If the company follows a similar pattern for its latest series, you can expect the next two puzzles to arrive sometime in early 2027.

items.title: The Witcher 3 Songs of the Past Expansion: Everything Revealed at gamescom ONL 2026
items.description: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Songs of the Past expansion got a proper reveal trailer at gamescom Opening Night Live 2026, and developer CD Projekt Red showed up to talk about its new chain weapon, the realm of Letten, and more.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Songs of the Past got a proper reveal trailer at gamescom Opening Night Live 2026, and developer CD Projekt Red showed up to talk about its new chain weapon, the realm of Letten, and more.

Geralt of Rivia helped close out ONL 2026 when the studio talked about how it plans to revisit its critically acclaimed 2015 RPG with new content next year. There's still much that hasn't been revealed, but this first showing finally teased what it will be like for players to revisit The Witcher 3 12 years after its original launch.

We'll get into all of the details that CD Projekt Red had to share, but first, the show had another surprise for viewers: a trailer. You can see the first The Witcher 3 Songs of the Past teaser below.

Get Over Here

So, what does the first Songs of the Past trailer tell us? Unfortunately, not much – at least at first glance. Geralt can first be seen approaching a tree decorated with lanterns before dancing in a camp with a partner who may not actually be there. Next, we're introduced to the moonlit skies and sun-kissed fields of Letten, the new realm where Songs of the Past takes place.

Geralt will find himself confronted with a new assortment of humans and monsters, and while that might be nothing new for a Witcher, the big bad whispering throughout the teaser might be. What might have most Witcher 3 fans the most excited, though, is the weapon featured toward the end of the video. The few seconds of footage showed Geralt using a chain to grapple and grapple an enemy before decapitating them. It looks like it could have been ripped right out of the hands of Mortal Kombat's Scorpion and seems to fit well in a Witcher's arsenal.

Welcome to Letten

An official description for the expansion teased what lies in Letten and its ties to the new story: "This idyllic land is rich in rural tradition and folklore, and its people enjoy a fulfilling life of bountiful harvests and lavish festivals. But a dark secret lurks just beneath the surface, and Geralt must overcome never-before-seen foes as he fights to overcome its long-dormant evil."

As revealed during the show, fans can officially wishlist Songs of the Past ahead of its eventual release. CD Projekt Red said the content will take players to the new realm of Letten, though what few sneak peeks we got of it seem to be tied to that trailer.

CD Projekt Red Talks Returning to The Witcher 3

Fans of The Witcher games and books will surely find plenty to pick apart while we wait for Songs of the Past to launch next year, but CD Projekt Red didn't want to stop there. Level design lead Miles Tost took the gamescom ONL stage to share more details about how the expansion builds on the original game.

"It's super cool," Tost said with a laugh. "We had this idea for one more story with Geralt for a while, but we couldn't quite figure out how to fit it into our busy schedules. Luckily, our friends from Fool's Theory came around, and they hired a bunch of old veteran Witcher 3 developers – including my mentor, Peter Gelenscer – and here we are today."

Tost noted that this is The Witcher 3 protagonist's last adventure before Ciri takes the torch in The Witcher 4 sometime in 2028. Giving Geralt a chain will help make his journey in Songs of the Past particularly memorable.

Chains from the books are back, i can't believe this man 😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/FXVYm6GEW9

— Kercy (@KdeKercy) August 25, 2026

"This chain is a weapon that is new in the game, but many people, perhaps hardcore Witcher fans, will realize that this is a weapon we first showed in The Witcher 1 intro," Tost continued, directing fans to head to the CD Projekt Red booth at gamescom to learn more.

Tost also had some words to share about Letten and how that environment will change things up for fans: "Letten is a whole new, unique region that has a unique identity, like the other regions in the game. It is filled with quests, new monsters, adventures and exploration – just like the things that Witcher fans love. But it's an almost uncannily idyllic place that, however, has a dark secret lurking just underneath the surface and, as it is a Witcher game, this kind of secret requires a true professional Witcher to solve."

Geralt is finally back. The Witcher 3 Songs of the Past may not have a release date, but it is still expected to launch sometime in 2027 for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. In the meantime, players can also look forward to The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered, which was also announced during gamescom ONL 2026.

We'll hopefully learn more about the surprise expansion in the months ahead. In the meantime, the developer also recently confirmed that the add-on will bring more Gwent to the game. You can also check out everything announced during ONL here.

Fans of The Witcher games and books will surely find plenty to pick apart while we wait for Songs of the Past to launch next year, but CD Projekt Red didn't want to stop there. Level design lead Miles Tost took the gamescom ONL stage to share more details about how the expansion builds on the original game.

"It's super cool," Tost said with a laugh. "We had this idea for one more story with Geralt for a while, but we couldn't quite figure out how to fit it into our busy schedules. Luckily, our friends from Fool's Theory came around, and they hired a bunch of old veteran Witcher 3 developers – including my mentor, Peter Gelenscer – and here we are today."

Tost noted that this is The Witcher 3 protagonist's last adventure before Ciri takes the torch in The Witcher 4 sometime in 2028. Giving Geralt a chain will help make his journey in Songs of the Past particularly memorable.

Chains from the books are back, i can't believe this man 😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/FXVYm6GEW9

— Kercy (@KdeKercy) August 25, 2026

"This chain is a weapon that is new in the game, but many people, perhaps hardcore Witcher fans, will realize that this is a weapon we first showed in The Witcher 1 intro," Tost continued, directing fans to head to the CD Projekt Red booth at gamescom to learn more.

But it's an almost uncannily idyllic place that, however, has a dark secret lurking just underneath the surface and, as it is a Witcher game, this kind of secret requires a true professional Witcher to solve."

Geralt is finally back. The Witcher 3 Songs of the Past may not have a release date, but it is still expected to launch sometime in 2027 for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. In the meantime, players can also look forward to The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered, which was also announced during gamescom ONL 2026.

We'll hopefully learn more about the surprise expansion in the months ahead. In the meantime, the developer also recently confirmed that the add-on will bring more Gwent to the game. You can also check out everything announced during ONL here.

items.title: Some Razer Gaming Gear Is Getting (Slightly Different) Translucent Green Options for Xbox's 25th Anniversary
items.description: Shortly after Microsoft announced a translucent green Xbox Series X, Razer joined in on the fun with a collection of Xbox-themed gaming mice and keyboards.
items.author: Wes Davis
items.content:
With Gamescom and the 25th anniversary translucent green Xbox Series X on the horizon (for those with the cash to nab one), perhaps it's time to start looking around for similarly see-through accessories. So, of course Razer has announced new Xbox 25th Anniversary Edition versions of its BlackWidow V4 75% Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, Basilisk V3 Pro 35K wireless gaming mouse, and Hammerhead V3 X Hyperspeed low-latency AirPods-like wireless earbuds.

These are the same devices we've come to know in the past. IGN called the BlackWidow V4 75 Razer's "most thoughtful" keyboard back in 2023; it's a less featureful version of the BlackWidow V4 75 Pro that sits on IGN's best gaming keyboards list.

Like the existing V4 75s, the Xbox 25th Anniversary Edition features RGB lighting and hot-swappable keys, only now it's got a see-through green shell and keys, as well as a Razer and Xbox 25 logo-emblazoned wrist rest. Also, at $210, it costs $20 more than plain black or white models, and $10 more than other versions, like the existing translucent, but slightly darker-colored Phantom Green.

Then there's the $180 Basilisk V3 Pro 35K mouse and the $120 Hammerhead V3 X Hyperspeed earbuds. The Basilisk V3 Pro 35K can work wired, but also works over Bluetooth and ships with a Razer HyperSpeed Wireless Dongle, and should be good for up to 210 hours of battery live via Bluetooth.

The Hammerhead V3 X Hyperspeed features 11mm drivers and a shape that's very reminiscent of the 3rd-gen AirPods Pro, only, you know, kind of a pukey, see-through green. Like their translucent keyboard cousin, they each come at a $20 premium compared to their black or white variants.

So, what say you? Do you like green mice and keebs?

Wes is a freelance writer (Freelance Wes, they call him) who has covered technology, gaming, and entertainment steadily since 2020 at Gizmodo, Tom's Hardware, Hardcore Gamer, and most recently, The Verge. Inside of him there are two wolves: one that thinks it wouldn't be so bad to start collecting game consoles again, and the other who also thinks this, but more strongly.

items.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Gets New Trailer at Gamescom 2026 Showing off Submarine Combat, Weapons, and More
items.description: Fans were treated to a new Final Fantasy 7 Revelation trailer at Gamescom’s Opening Night Live showcase, where we saw more of The Weapons, submarine combat, and more.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Fans were treated to a new Final Fantasy 7 Revelation trailer at Gamescom’s Opening Night Live showcase, where we saw more of The Weapons, a submarine combat section, and more.

The trailer opens up with Rufus Shinra sharing a public service announcement on the Shinra News Network regarding the looming Meteor and the Weapons, assuring citizens that humanity will “reign supreme” over these obstacles.

We get to see one of these Weapons wreaking havoc on Shinra soldiers, as well as special shots of the Ruby Weapon, Emerald Weapon, and the Ultima Weapon.

Gameplay footage showing Tifa wearing the Black Mage class outfit was is shown off, as well as a prerendered cutscene showing the Highwind facing off with a Weapon. We even get to see the inside of the submarine with the Huge Materia smack in the middle, along with an underwater combat section that shows the party navigating through the ocean as the submarine dodges attacks.

Footage of the team parachuting down from the Highwind and riding chocobos through the world is also included, as well as Yuffie exploring what seems to be Wutai, making for an extremely hype trailer that is leaving fans more excited than ever.

Most of the dialogue in the trailer centered around the Weapons, with Vincent Valentine explaining in a voiceover that "the Planet sees us as another threat to her well-being, and rightfully so."

"You call 'em planetary warriors," Cid says. "But I call 'em weapons of mass destruction!"

It remains to be seen if these featured Weapons will be normal bosses or super bosses, in keeping with the original game. Unfortunately, no specific release date was revealed, either. Spring 2027 is still the ongoing release window for the game, which will release simultaneously on PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (via Steam, Epic Games Store, and Xbox PC.

This is the latest look we've gotten at FFVII Revelation following the trailers that were shown at Summer Game Fest earlier this year, where we were reintroduced to the Highwind. Using the airship, Cloud and company will be able to traverse all across the planet, dropping down via parachutes to explore to your heart's content.

It also introduced the FITS system, which allows each character to change their playstyle based on Final Fantasy jobs. Speaking of gameplay, yes, you'll get the chance to play the gunslinging Vincent Valentine and even transform into the Galian Beast.

As yet, not much else has been revealed about the game, but director Naoki Hamaguchi has publicly stated that he wants to integrate many of the Final Fantasy VII spin-off properties into its ultimate ending.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered Launches September as a Free Upgrade for Existing Owners
items.description: CD Projekt Red has announced The Witcher 3 Remastered, coming as a free upgrade to all owners next month.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
CD Projekt Red has announced The Witcher 3 Remastered, coming as a free upgrade to all owners on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S next month on September 29.

In a stunning conclusion to Gamescom's Opening Night Live, the developer confirmed a list of additional features coming to the game's Remastered version as well as notably enhanced visuals, which we've listed out below.

There's no upgrade to the game's current Switch 1 version, though a separate Switch 2-native version of The Witcher 3 Remastered will be sold, and owners of the Switch 1 version will be able to claim this free. The remastered game will also be sold on PC via Battle.net for the first time, where it will unlock a Geralt-themed skin in Diablo 4.

The Witcher 3 Remastered — and the current game, as of today — will also include access to the game's first two expansions at no additional cost. Of course, all of this precedes the arrival of the upcoming Songs of the Past, The Witcher 3's third expansion, due in 2027. For a detailed look at what we saw of that this evening, we have you covered right here.

Everything new coming to The Witcher 3 Remastered

Major features include tweaked combat, improved traversal and movement, revamped mount handling, enhanced monster behaviors, a skill tree revamp, armor transmog, an expanded photo mode, new finishers and much more.

Other additions include the long-awaited cross-platform mod support, new quest tracking, immersive meditation, refined animations, UI improvements, a looting rework, refreshed motion blur, new accessibility features, a tutorial modernization, HDR improvements, a foliage shading rework, ray-tracing improvements, a global lighting reork, new shading model, subsurface scattering, and a new tone mapper.

PlayStation 5 Pro support, plus Xbox Play Anywhere and unspecified Nintendo Switch 2 "exclusive features" were also mentioned, as were Nvidia DLSS 4.5, AMD FSR 4, Intel XESS 2.0, path tracing and ray reconstruction on PC, native DX12 and rendering parallelization. There will even be ray-traced hair.

Yesterday it was confirmed that Songs of the Past will contain more Gwent, the franchise's compulsive card game.

As previously confirmed, there was no sign of The Witcher 4 tonight — though none was expected. Yesterday, we gained confirmation that the highly-anticipated Ciri-starring sequel is targeting a 2028 release window, and was very much still in the oven at present.

"Our team here at CD Projekt Red HQ is hard at work on a brand new saga, one with Ciri at the helm," CD Projekt Red joint CEO Michał Nowakowski said previously. "We have more than 500 incredibly talented developers working to create something truly special for you. The Witcher 4 features a huge and immersive open world, intense and action-packed gameplay, and a deep, impactful story that we hope will stay with you for a long time. Simply put, this is our biggest, boldest, and most ambitious game to date.

"Now I know you're eager to learn when it's coming. That's the question we're hearing from you all the time. So while we're not showing The Witcher 4 at the event, and we're not ready to share an exact date, I can tell you this: The Witcher 4 is targeting a 2028 release window.

"I know it's a bit of a wait and you'd love to play it sooner, but let the team cook. It will be worth the wait. Until then, there will be plenty more of The Witcher to come, including Songs of the Past when it launches in 2027. And you can be sure gamescom is also in our plans for the coming years."

Catch up on all of tonight's announcements in our roundup of everything revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: LEGO Skylines Announced at Gamescom
items.description: A new LEGO city builder known as LEGO Skylines has been announced at Gamescom.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
A new LEGO city builder known as LEGO Skylines has been announced at Gamescom.

After a leak earlier this summer, Paradox Interactive has officially announced a LEGO version of its beloved city builder series, Cities: Skylines. Developed by Iceflake Studios, LEGO Skylines aims to allow players to build functional and logical cities, as you would in other city builders, but also push them to make something more creative and whimsical. One such example provided by the team behind the game is putting a bakery on every corner of the city, which can produce donuts using wheat provided by farmers from elsewhere in your city.

Using the creativity and imagination of the LEGO brand, LEGO Skylines players will be able to build the city of their dreams — not just maintain a realistic, functioning city, but one that lets them try outlandish and absurd ideas using LEGO bricks and decorations. The game promises a "frankly absurd amount of buildings, decorations, and other cool stuff" to build cities.

“Building and creativity have always been at the heart of the LEGO experience, but LEGO Skylines takes us into completely new territory,” said Fredrik Löving, SVP, Global Head of game at the LEGO Group. “Together with Paradox Interactive and Iceflake Studios, we have brought the LEGO experience to one of the world's most beloved gaming genres. From the beginning, our ambition wasn’t just to make a LEGO city-builder, it was to create a game that is considered among the best in the genre. Whether players dream of building a bustling metropolis, a quirky seaside town, or something nobody has imagined before, LEGO Skylines gives them the creative freedom and depth to make it happen.”

All in all, it sounds like a really charming and fun city builder. There's no release date for LEGO Skylines at the moment, but it will be available on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC when it comes out.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Path of Exile 2 Release Date Sets 1.0 Launch in December 2026
items.description: Grinding Gear Games has announced Path of Exile 2 1.0 has a December release date.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Grinding Gear Games has announced Path of Exile 2 1.0 has a December release date.

The studio announced the long-awaited schedule update with a trailer that premiered at gamescom Opening Night Live (ONL) 2026, confirming plans to bring its free-to-play action-RPG to PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S December 11, 2026. The footage mixed together Path of Exile 2 gameplay with cinematics while promising that players will finally get their hands on a complete build just in time for the holidays.

Grinding Gear revealed more information on its website, directing interested fans to register for more information. Those who do can unlock exclusive rewards.

"Path of Exile 2 is a next-generation action RPG from Grinding Gear Games, featuring co-op for up to six players," an official description on its Steam page said. "Path of Exile 2 takes place in the land of Wraeclast, a dark continent populated by unique cultures, ancient secrets, and monstrous dangers. A sinister threat, long thought destroyed, has begun creeping back on the edge of civilisation, driving people mad and sickening the land with Corruption."

Grinding Gear first launched Path of Exile 2 in an early access state in December 2024. All the buildup led to a massive launch on Steam, and now, after a few years of ups and downs, the full launch will finally bring the team's vision for launch to life. Part of that vision includes the Duelist, a new class showcased in today's trailer that will be available at launch.

IGN called Path of Exile 2 early access "Great" in our 8/10 review. Even in its unrefined state at the time, we said its "redefined action and surprisingly fleshed-out endgame" got things off to a good start. While we wait for updates, be sure to check out everything announced at gamescom ONL 2026.

items.title: Backrooms Is Officially Coming to HBO Max in September
items.description: Backrooms officially has a streaming release date.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Backrooms officially has a streaming release date.

The breakout horror movie directed by 21-year-old-Kane Parsons is coming to HBO Max on Friday, September 25. It will debut on HBO linear channels the following day at 8pm ET.

The streaming release comes just under four months after Backrooms was initially released in theaters, where it dominated the box office. It grossed over $80 million in its opening weekend and quickly become A24’s highest-grossing movie of all time. It finished its theatrical run at just shy of $400 million globally, and remains one of the highest-grossing movies of the year so far.

Toward the end of its stint in theaters, Backrooms received became available to watch in extended “Everything Must Go” screenings, featuring over 15 minutes of extra footage in the style of Parsons’ original YouTube series. That extra footage is already available to watch on YouTube for free, and it's unclear whether it'll be added to HBO Max in any capacity.

For now, Backrooms is available to rent or buy digitally from platforms like Prime Video. A spread of 4K Blu-rays with "over three hours of special features" are also available to buy from the A24 Shop.

We were pretty big fans of Backrooms, with critic Lex Briscuso describing it as “a truly terrifying cinematic rabbit hole” in her 8/10 review for IGN. It's one of our best-reviewed movies of the year so far, and generally currently sits at an 87% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

All in all, it should come as no surprise that there are already talks of a potential sequel, though Parsons has also expressed his interest in adapting the iconic 2007 Valve game, Portal. Other creepypasta-inspired movies have also been getting the green light since the Backrooms success, most notably a Siren Head movie helmed by Weapons' and the upcoming Resident Evil movie's director, Zach Cregger.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who, when she isn't following streaming news, spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

items.title: Crimson Desert Is Becoming Crimson Desert Enhanced for Free
items.description: Pearl Abyss has announced Crimson Desert Enhanced, a new version of the game with additional story, available free to all players.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Pearl Abyss has announced Crimson Desert Enhanced, a new version of the game with additional story, available free to all players.

Simply update the game to version 2.00.00 and Crimson Desert Enhanced will be yours, Pearl Abyss has said. So, to be clear, it is just a fresh patch for the existing game — but one that Pearl Abyss feels is so substantial that it warrants an updated title for the full game.

Crimson Desert Enhanced adds new cutscenes and story moments throughout the main questline, plus voiceover support so you can enjoy the game's narrative in German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese and Japanese.

Pearl Abyss previously promised a summer roadmap of content that includes improvements to the core narrative – a recurring criticism of the game at launch. And of course, the Enhanced edition will include all existing updates to the game — and there have been a lot, with new bits and pieces every few weeks.

All of this comes ahead of the game's first paid DLC, due this year, and a Nintendo Switch 2 release, expected in early 2027. Research on multiplayer modes and potential sequels is also underway, following the game's breakout success so far.

Crimson Desert launched back in March 19 and was an instant hit for Pearl Abyss. Less than three months after launch, Crimson Desert crossed the 6 million copies sold mark.

Catch up on all of tonight's announcements in our roundup of everything revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026.

items.title: Rainbow Six Tactics Features Optional Permadeath, Ironman Mode
items.description: Ubisoft just announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player turn-based tactics game starring 15 fan-favorite Operators from the popular long-running multiplayer first-person shooter Rainbow Six Siege. I had the chance to talk to Tactics game director Martial Potron about creating the first single-player Rainbow Six game since Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008, including his thoughts on other franchises that have successfully pivoted genres, the importance of being a tactics game first, and more.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Ubisoft just announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player turn-based tactics game starring 15 fan-favorite Operators from the popular long-running multiplayer first-person shooter Rainbow Six Siege. I had the chance to talk to Tactics game director Martial Potron about creating the first single-player Rainbow Six game since Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008, including his thoughts on other franchises that have successfully pivoted genres, the importance of being a tactics game first, and more.

First, on that tactics-genre staple of permadeath, Potron said, "We know it’s a must-have for tactical fans. R6T features optional permadeath, as well as an Ironman mode. In practical terms, Operators who are too severely injured can be permanently unavailable for the rest of the campaign. Players can enable it at any difficulty level, so they can experience the added tension of risking to lose an operator on an easier setting. It dramatically changes the way you play, because operators are unique and not replaceable. Losing a favourite or highly progressed Operator forces players to adapt their strategy and rethink squad composition."

I reference Gears Tactics as another big action franchise that made a pretty successful pivot to tactics, and Potron didn't do the usual move of not mentioning anyone else's game by name, and offered this when I asked about lessons learned from other games that have dipped their toes in the tactics waters: "The key lesson is that the game must first succeed on its own terms," he said. "Tactical-game fans have very high expectations, so R6 Tactics has to stand as a strong tactics game before it can succeed as a Rainbow Six game. Our franchise competitors that ventured into the tactics genre succeeded because they combined strong franchises with excellent design, canon storytelling, and production values.

"R6 Tactics has to stand as a strong tactics game before it can succeed as a Rainbow Six game."

"The second lesson is that a genre shift works best when it translates the franchise identity rather than simply reskinning another formula. Gears Tactics, for example, adapted executions and emergence holes to recreate the pace and aggression of Gears. Despite being turn-based, the game still felt unmistakably like Gears.

"Regarding Rainbow Six, one might think it’ll be a challenge to adapt a shooter, where much of the fun comes from aiming, reacting, and executing. But the Rainbow Franchise fortunately already have this ideal of being the Smart Shooter, where thinking before acting is paramount. Our job is not to impose tactics on Rainbow Six, but to express the tactical thinking that has always defined it through a new genre. So for us, the transition was smooth as all the elements were already there. Shooting, reconnaissance, breaching, gadgets, and coordination cannot feel like generic tactics mechanics; each decision must feel specifically like Rainbow Six."

Potron also told me that there are lots of references to the entire series in Tactics. "The planning phase of the original Rainbow Six was a key inspiration for one of our main features: the Breach. Players can coordinate an assault on a heavily defended location by choosing entry points (doors, windows, or any destructible wall); assigning operators to them, and synchronizing explosives, grenades, and shots to neutralize as many enemies as possible before turn-based combat resumes. It’s our modern take on this feature of the early games.

"There are other nods throughout Tactics as well. At the start of missions, players choose insertion points that shape their approach and the risks they take. On the narrative side, rebuilding Rainbow after its destruction in Siege’s Year 10 also allowed us to reconnect with the wider story of the franchise, including Paul Bishop from Rainbow Six Vegas 2. We worked closely with the Rainbow team in Montreal to make sure everything was properly tied together. So yes, we drew from the entire history of Rainbow Six, from the earliest games to Vegas and Siege, to create both gameplay and narrative touchstones."

Finally, I asked Potron what from Siege translated well to a tactics game and what required clever reintrpretation. He went right to one of Siege's signature features for the former: destruction. "In most tactical games, players must flank, cover and work with existing lines of sight. Here, they can create new paths and firing angles by destroying walls and covers. But enemies can do the same, which means no position is completely safe. This fundamentally changes how players approach the battlefield.

"A single plan can contain up to twelve decisions before the player presses 'Execute.'"

"Breach planning, an iconic feature of classic Rainbow Six, was also at the heart of our reflection. Players select entry points, coordinate four operators, assign grenades and abilities, and prioritize dangerous targets. A single plan can contain up to twelve decisions before the player presses “Execute.” Balancing that depth with accessibility—and then turning all those synchronized actions into one clear, cinematic sequence—required considerable iteration.

"The biggest reinterpretation was translating Siege’s uncertainty into a turn-based format. In Siege, danger often comes from not knowing what is behind a wall, a corner, or a barricade. In R6 Tactics, our precise & dynamic fog-of-war system recreates that tension. Careful scouting and drones become essential before breaching. The key was balancing tension with fairness, so hidden threats remain dangerous without becoming frustrating."

Rainbow Six Tactics is due out next year for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Commodore Computer Premieres at Gamescom, and It's Up for Preorder Now
items.description: The retro-futurism of Cyberpunk 2077 meets the retro computerism of the modern Commodore 64.
items.author: Seth G. Macy
items.content:
When I reviewed the Commodore 64 Ultimate, I honestly couldn't believe just how perfect it was. It surprised me in ways I didn't expect, and it's truly the result of a love and respect for the brand. It's why I gave the C64 Ultimate a 10 in my review. It's a thing of beauty, and now Commodore has officially unveiled a gorgeous new update in collaboration with CD Projekt Red: The Commodore 77.

The case itself is gorgeous, with the plate on the function keys now made of brushed metal. That's not a "brushed metal" finish, by the way: it's actually brushed metal. The rest of the case has been colored to match the Cyberpunk style, the Commodore 64 badge has been replaced with a Commodore 77 badge, and there are other changes that have to be seen to really be appreciated. The entire case has a weathered, suitably cyberpunk look to it, but just like with humans, it's what's inside that counts.

Aside from the new look, the Commodore 77 can now run at a blistering 77Mhz, compared to the 1Mhz of the original Commodore 64. There's also 77MB of system RAM compared to the original Ultimate's 16MB. While this new speed and power is pretty impressive (for the 1980s), it does run the risk of making some of your hand-written programs run impossibly fast, but you can toggle the higher speed off and on in the menus.

Hey, speaking of menus, the C77 also has a "custom Cyberpunk 2077 themed Commodore 77 BASIC 2.0 boot screen", which continues the overall Cyberpunk feel. The famous spiral-bound manual that's shipped with each Commodore 64 has also gotten a Cyberpunk facelift, and comes "packed with lore and exclusive Cyberpunk 2077-themed type-in BASIC programs." It's exactly the kind of thing old heads like me crave.

Each Commodore 77 ships with a shard-inspired Arasaka cartridge containing a demo created by Polish demo group Arise, with the soundtrack composed by chiptune artist LukHash. This is an old-school computer demo, the sort of thing hackers used to distribute to show off their chops. I've seen it. It's incredible. It's hard to believe what people can do with such limited computational power, but the soundtrack benefits enormously from the 24-track stereo SID chip that's part of the Ultimate.

Given how well Commodore did with its modern debut, I have no doubt in my mind the C77 is going to be similarly awesome, especially given the pedigree of its collaboration. Did I mention it comes with stickers and pins and in "collectible themed packaging?"

Oh, and it has LED lights that dance to the music on the demo. It's kind of everything I didn't even know I wanted.

Preorders are live at Commodore's website for $377, with an expected release date sometime next year. I, for one, welcome our CyberPunk and Commodore retro future.

items.title: Exodus Release Date Revealed, the Mass Effect-Like RPG Is Coming in April
items.description: Exodus shares plenty of similarities with Mass Effect and seems to be filling the sci-fi RPG void; you won't have to wait long to play it, too.
items.author: Michael Higham
items.content:
During gamescom's Opening Night Live, developer Archetype Entertainment revealed the release date for its Mass Effect-like spacefaring RPG: Exodus is launching on April 7, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam and Epic Games Store. It premiered a new cinematic trailer that showcased new characters and gameplay centered around an intelligent octopus who pilots a mech suit.

Her name is Salt and she is one of several party members you'll gather in Exodus. She is an Awakened, which in the universe of Exodus are hyper-intelligent animals and wildlife who can communicate with humans. Salt will be a long-range sniper who can use an ink smokescreen to provide cover in combat. The trailer hits heavier beats that tease some of its story elements – while Salt gives the main character Jun hard time and tends to be confrontational, she's emotionally driven to protect her species and homeworld.

One of the major hooks of Exodus is the scientific incorporation of time dilation and how it'll affect the story. In true RPG fashion, it'll have player choices that can change outcomes and you'll have a crew to accompany you (a Traveler known as Jun) along the interstallar journey where humanity had to flee Earth and find a new home in the great expanse.

Veteran narrative designer and writer Drew Karpyshyn is the narrative director on Exodus. If you're not familiar, he worked on some of BioWare's most critically acclaimed games serving as senior writer on Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and lead writer on Mass Effect.

Exodus was first revealed during The Game Awards 2023 and made headlines for having famed actor Matthew McCounghey voicing the trailer and playing a character in the game. There was an extended 20-minute gameplay reveal back in June that showcased the action RPG combat, which is very reminescent of Mass Effect with its shooting mechanics and commanding of party member abilities – it also shares a particular sci-fi aesthetic with the BioWare series. Archtype Entertainment has been working under Wizards of the Coast since 2020 and it won't be long until we can finally play what its been working on.

items.title: Game of Thrones: War for Westeros Trailer Features The Night King on the Iron Throne
items.description: Here's a first proper look at gameplay from Game of Thrones: War for Westeros, the upcoming real-time strategy title that lets you conqueror the Seven Kingdoms as one of numerous factions.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Here's a first proper look at gameplay from Game of Thrones: War for Westeros, the upcoming real-time strategy title that lets you conqueror the Seven Kingdoms as one of numerous factions.

Fresh from Gamescom's Opening Night Live broadcast, we have word that Game of Thrones: War for Westeros will launch in early 2027 and have a playable beta before release. More details on exactly when you'll be able to play will follow later this year.

Footage shown today included numerous heroes from the HBO series in action, including Jon Snow, Jaime Lannister, Daenerys Targaryen and the Night King — who ends the trailer sat firmly upon the Iron Throne. Oh dear!

Thankfully you will have your own chance to rewrite Game of Thrones' climactic battle for the Seven Kingdoms as all sorts of factions, and deploy custom units in real-time skirmish battles. A press release accompanying today's reveal also includes mention of Robb Stark, Tywin Lannister and — curiously — both Ghost and Grey Wind.

Alongside direwolves, specific armies will be able to deploy giants, dragons, elephants, and that green fire which destroyed half of King's Landing.

Last month, Game of Thrones: War for Westeros developer PlaySide Studios pushed back the game's release window from 2026 into early 2027, explaining that the extra breathing room "gives us the time needed to continue building towards that goal and ensure that the game reaches the high level of quality we are aiming for."

"We remain unwavering in our mission to deliver a real-time strategy game set in the world of Westeros that meets the expectations of both RTS players and Game of Thrones fans," PlaySide added. "Thank you for your patience and continued support. We know the wait has been long, and we do not take your support for granted."

Catch up on all of tonight's announcements in our roundup of everything revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social
